newsitem.title: USA: Stocks buoyed by strong earnings.
newsitem.headline: Stocks buoyed by strong earnings.

text.p: Stocks were moderately higher Thursday after profit-taking erased much of the gains scored in an early rally sparked by strong earnings reports, particularly from technology companies.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 9.63 points at 6,736.51 following a late morning gain of more than 50 points.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 12-10 on active volume of 308 million shares on the NYSE.
The Nasdaq Composite index, which is heavily weighted with high technology stocks, was up 7.26 points at 1,340.79. The American Stock Exchange index was up 1.44 at 587.92.
"Earnings are coming in better than expected, most remarkably in the high tech sector," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp.

Earnings winners among the techs included Sun Microsystems Inc., which rose 3 to 31-1/4 and Xilinx Inc., up 4-7/8 at 42-1/2 after they both reported upbeat results after Wednesday's close. Digital Equipment Corp. gained 3-3/4 to 37-7/8 on strong profits for the latest quarter.

"Yesterday it was buy on the rumour and sell on the news. Today, techs are rebounding," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "The bottom line is that people have an appetite for tech issues. Also for stocks in general, but the techs in particular."

"If there is a sector of the economy that will to do well in 1997, it's high techs," Johnson said. "Spending on computers and peripherals should grow at a pace of no less than 15 percent, and that's a modest estimate. No other sector will do that well. The question is which companies will participate and how much they will take to the bottom line."
The Dow index seemed to draw most of its strength from a rally in the stock of Eastman Kodak Co., which rose 4-1/8 to 85-3/8 after the company posted higher earnings.
Playboy Entertainment Inc. gained 1 to 10-5/8 after the company said it expected to report higher profits for the latest quarter.
Stocks ignored weakness in the bond market.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond lost 11/32, raising its yield to 6.82 percent from 6.79 percent at Wednesday's close. The bond's price moves in the opposite direction of its yield.
